column4: copyThenRemove(src, dst, remover) replaces copyTree + deleteTree: every removal's answer is kept (removeTree answers what could not be removed, with why). A held file means the ORIGINAL is already part-removed and the copy is the only whole mod, so the finding's suggested fix (delete the copy and throw) would have lost the files removed before it: instead what was removed is put back from the copy, then the copy goes, and the move is refused naming the held files - nothing moved, one whole mod. If putting back fails the copy is kept and the message says where it is. A copy that fails part way is removed before the error. The remover is a parameter (Files::delete in the program) so the suite can hand it a held file; this machine runs as root, where permissions cannot make one. Proven in the dev tree; port pending.

column4: BLOCKED ON THE DUMP AND AN IN-GAME CHECK. Each 0x38 mesh header holds a centre vector (+0x24, 3 floats) and a pointer to a bounding-box block (+0x34). Writing either correctly needs their meaning measured on retail models - is the centre the vertex box's middle, what the block holds and in what order - and whether the engine culls by them is an in-game question. The one model here, DummyBCH3DModel, has no block (pointer 0) and a zero centre over a -1..1 cube (measured, scratch MeshBounds probe), so it cannot answer either. Guessing a layout and writing it into every edited mesh could break models that work today. NEXT STEP WITH THE DUMP: measure centre vs vertex box and the block over the 857 FieldData models; if the centre is the box middle and the block an AABB/OBB, recompute both in BchMapModel's geometry writers and have BchModelVerifier check them; OWNER: walk a moved/resized region at grazing angles to see whether geometry outside the old box disappears. CLOSED 2026-10-09 by measuring on the dump - and the row's layout was wrong. Over all 14,117 retail FieldData meshes: the centre is at +0x20, not +0x24, and +0x34 points not at a box but at the mesh's metadata dictionary, which names an 'OBBox' (centre, a 3x3 orientation stored row-major with the axes in its COLUMNS, full size) and a '$BBoxMinMax'. The header centre IS the OBBox centre and every vertex lies inside the OBBox in all 14,112 that decode; $BBoxMinMax is the mesh's box in only 3,363 (the model's in 1,090, neither in 9,145, absent from 519), so it is neither checked nor written. Every writer now refits a box its moved vertices left - setVertexPositions, translate and the setMeshGeometries rebuild under setMeshGeometry, appendGeometry and the blank canvas - keeping the exporter's axes and measuring centre and extents along them; a box that still holds its mesh is left byte for byte.
